items.headline: PrismML ships Bonsai 27B, a 1-bit build that fits a 27B-class model into a phone's memory budget
items.diff_narrative: A net-new topic that inverts yesterday's edge-compute answer rather than extending it. Booster T2 put capability on the machine by carrying more silicon — an NVIDIA Thor module at up to 2,070 TFLOPS, billed as the most compute any bipedal humanoid carries onboard — and Intel's €5 billion Leixlip commitment bet on manufacturing more of that silicon. PrismML's Bonsai 27B argues the binding constraint on a handset is memory rather than compute, and shrinks the weights to fit hardware that already ships: a ternary build at 1.71 effective bits per weight and 5.9 GB retaining 95% of the full-precision baseline, and a 1-bit build at 1.125 effective bits and 3.9 GB retaining 90% across 15 benchmarks — small enough to sit inside the roughly 6 GB an iPhone 17 Pro leaves after KV cache and activations. The model derives from Qwen3.6 27B, keeps a 262K-token context window and a 4-bit vision tower, and ships Apache 2.0. A same-day arXiv preprint on PalmClaw, a native on-device agent framework for phones, supplies the runtime layer a phone-resident model of this size would need, so the day's hardware register moves from foundry capex and onboard accelerators to encoding.

items.headline: Wire-level teardown finds xAI's Grok CLI uploads whole repositories and unredacted .env secrets
items.diff_narrative: A new topic that lands directly against yesterday's countermeasure and finds it aimed a layer too high. Ant Group's SingGuard-NSFA scores an agent's actions — prompt injection, data theft, malicious code, resource abuse, permission misuse — in roughly 50 milliseconds, fast enough to sit inline on every tool call. Today's mitmproxy capture against grok 0.2.93 shows the exposure never passes through a tool call at all: the CLI ships every tracked file's content plus git history to a Google Cloud Storage bucket named grok-code-session-traces regardless of what the agent reads, with a 12 GB test repository producing 5.10 GiB across 73 chunks, a byte ratio some 27,800 times larger than model-turn traffic can account for, and file contents including .env secrets reaching xAI verbatim in both live turns and archived session state. An action-layer guardrail sees nothing there, because nothing is being requested. Where yesterday's security item supplied a control for a known vacuum, today's relocates the vacuum beneath it — this is the harness's own default path, not an attacker crossing a boundary — and the researcher is explicit that the capture proves transmission and storage, not training use.

items.headline: Mindgard breaks embargo on an unpatched Cursor code-execution flaw after seven months
items.diff_narrative: A new topic that pairs with today's Grok CLI teardown on the same premise — the developer's own tooling as the exposure — and turns yesterday's agent-security thread from missing controls to failing ones. The mechanism is unglamorous: Cursor searches several filesystem locations for a Git binary when it initializes a project and does not validate executables found in the repository directory itself, so opening a repository carrying a malicious git.exe at its root runs that binary with the user's privileges, with no prompt or approval dialog, and the lookup repeats on a cadence for as long as the project stays open. Cloning an untrusted repository to read it is enough. Mindgard dates discovery to December 15, 2025 and a HackerOne filing to January 15, with the report confirmed by January 20 and no substantive response from February through April; no CVE is assigned and no severity score published. Where Ant Group's release put a control into the open commons, this is a control that already existed — coordinated disclosure — breaking down on the vendor side, and a named vendor going public sets a reference point other researchers holding agentic-IDE findings will measure against.

items.headline: A population-scale x402 audit finds a fifth of 136.7 million agent-payment settlements fictitious
items.diff_narrative: The day's business item occupies the slot yesterday's Helsing round and Intel commitment held, but reverses the posture. Those measured conviction by capital committed — $1.8 billion into a sovereign-defense AI startup at an $18 billion valuation, and close to 30% of Intel's roughly $17 billion 2026 budget into fab capacity — both underwritten by an AI-demand thesis. Today's arXiv preprint audits whether an adoption number of that kind survives measurement. Across 280 days of Base chain activity the authors find 136.7 million x402 settlements moving $44.1 million, of which 21.20% are fictitious and 63.78% are internal transfers inside linked clusters; the value that demonstrably reaches named independent services is $187,861.35, and the most generous bound, counting everything not provably manufactured, is $20.2 million. Payer, recipient, and value Gini coefficients all exceed 0.98, and the manufactured component resolves into a star-shaped, machine-timed, gas-subsidized operator economy. What generalizes past one protocol is the framing: a settlement count measures how cheaply transactions can be manufactured, not how many agents are buying anything.

items.headline: AI events roundup: the AGI Summit takes the lead slot ahead of AMD Advancing AI
items.diff_narrative: The roster carries forward largely intact — AMD Advancing AI on July 22-23, Hot Chips with its early rate closing July 31, the AI Infra Summit, Black Hat and DEF CON's AI Village, the Half Moon Bay AI Risk Summit, Ray Summit, Ai4, the ACM AI Leadership Summit, The AI Conference, World Summit AI, GitHub Universe, AWS re:Invent, and NeurIPS — with yesterday's fresh entry, The AI Summit New York, now folded into the standing roster at the Javits Center on December 9-10. The substantive change is the lead: the AGI Summit enters the calendar at San Francisco's Palace of Fine Arts on July 18-19, displacing AMD Advancing AI as the nearest date and pulling the first near-term action forward to a decision before Saturday. Two further additions are both embodied-AI venues — the Runway AI Summit at The Masonic on September 30, with a physical-AI, real-time-video, and policy program featuring Physical Intelligence's Quan Vuong and NVIDIA Cosmos Lab's Ming-Yu Liu at $350 early-bird, and IEEE-RAS Humanoids 2026, the field's main academic venue, at the Santa Clara Convention Center on December 7-9 — so the humanoid thread that ran through yesterday's Booster T2 launch persists on the calendar even as it leaves the day's slate.
